name: Red Pill
qaNote: Reference inspected. Preserve swept brown hair, beard, red leather jacket, black shirt/trousers, silver jewelry and red/black sneakers. Review one continuous sound-pulse journey, exact title spelling, microphone continuity and cyan gaps through speaker rings. No spoken dialogue or political slogans.
choreography:
IDENTITY: exact adult light-skinned man with swept-back dark brown hair, short beard, glossy red leather jacket over a black shirt, dark trousers, silver dog tags and trouser chain, red-and-black sneakers, black handheld microphone. His red energy graphics are finite crimson sound strokes, never opaque backdrop panels.
0–1.2s: establish his whole body, microphone held at chest height, other hand pointing with supreme confidence. He taps the microphone twice, no speech. The second tap kicks out a small sharp crimson sound ring. Camera abruptly pulls back to reveal three enormous circular assemblies of black speaker cones suspended in a deep thirty-foot tunnel, with open pure-cyan centers and generous cyan between every object.
1.2–3.2s: race beside that one ring as it ricochets from one speaker assembly to the next. Each successive speaker flexes hugely and doubles the ring's size, creating a visible accelerating feedback relay. Tight dynamic perspective: first speaker at hand scale, last speaker larger than the man. The original character remains one person, visible at the far origin, no clones or chanting mouths.
3.2–4.8s: the colossal returning sound wave rushes toward him. He catches its rhythm with a precise microphone-down gesture, then jabs the mic forward like a conductor. The wave reverses and barrels through all three speaker assemblies, telescoping them together into one small crumpled speaker cube with a huge bounded ivory-and-crimson pressure star. One clear dominant contact beat, powerful scale change, cyan around the blast. The deafening buildup ends in a sharp sudden silence.
4.8–6s: snap close-up on his smug face, jacket collar fluttering. Exact title ECHO CHAMBER slams into the lower composition with a heavy bass impact, away from his face.
6–8s: return to a complete readable hero pose. The tiny speaker cube floats beside his shoulder. He gives the mic one satisfied tap; the cube emits a pathetic rubbery squeak and his eyebrow twitches. Hold that reaction. Sound is percussive mic taps, accelerating resonant pulses, huge compressed bass hit, abrupt hush, title slam and one tiny squeak. Absolutely no speech, narration, chanting or music.

name: Redneck
qaNote: Reference inspected. Preserve cap, mullet, goatee, torn red plaid shirt, white undershirt, dirty blue jeans, work boots and adjustable wrench. Existing small costume logos stay; no added motif. Review engine assembly readability in five seconds, glove-free hand/wrench grip, jeans chroma key and settled full-body ending.
choreography:
IDENTITY: exact adult man with brown mullet, short goatee and mischievous grin, red-and-white trucker cap, torn open red/black plaid shirt, white undershirt, weathered baggy blue jeans, heavy brown work boots, tool pouch and large steel adjustable wrench. Preserve existing costume markings as small physical details; do not invent additional badges or power symbols.
0–0.7s: complete character beside a sputtering exposed engine suspended on cyan, roughly his torso size. Three disconnected dirty charcoal smoke puffs cough from it. He narrows his eyes, seats the wrench on its central nut, and cracks a confident grin.
0.7–2.5s: one furious wrench turn triggers an outrageous EXPLODED MECHANICAL VIEW: camera rockets backward as pistons, gears and casing fly outward into a huge coherent spiral around him, thirty feet across. He stays at the center holding the original wrench, one continuous action. A second hard wrist turn reverses the spiral: all parts slam back together in clean sequential clacks into a towering gleaming hot-rod engine. Bright ivory starbursts at the assembly contacts, pure cyan clearly visible between separated parts. No building, garage or floor.
2.5–3.5s: he gives the final nut a tiny additional quarter-turn. The huge engine answers with one thunderous exhaust pulse that blasts the dirty smoke knots completely away, red plaid tails snapping in the air. Exact title FIX IT YOURSELF slams across the lower composition on that dominant mechanical BOOM, without covering his face. The engine is repaired and clean, not destroyed.
3.5–5s: camera whips back to his complete proud stance, wrench over shoulder and restored engine beside him. One spare bolt drops neatly into his free palm. He studies it, shrugs and pockets it, ending on his grin. SFX: initial sickly sputter, rapid metallic expansion and gear ratchets, cascading assembly CLACKS, one enormous engine ignition, title impact, little bolt clink. No music or voice. Choreograph for five seconds with distinct readable beats, not sped-up footage.

name: Redneck Evil
qaNote: Reference inspected. Preserve cap, long messy hair, torn vest/overalls, tattoos, heavy boots and chained axe. The reference has distressed dark-red marks; do not add injury or gore. Review continuous chain topology, bounded orange flame, clear first-to-second target relay and stable character silhouette.
choreography:
IDENTITY: exact rugged adult man from reference with long tangled brown hair, scruffy beard, stained red/cream trucker cap, ragged dark sleeveless vest, patched torn gray overalls, tattoos, leather wrist bands, work boots and heavy chained axe. Keep the distressed costume and prop shapes; introduce no new wounds or gore. Existing printed costume marks remain fixed details, never new captions.
0–1.2s: whole-body low-angle shot. He jerks the chained axe off his shoulder and starts one fast overhead orbit, loose chain drawing a huge elliptical arc. At the metal head, one tiny orange ember catches. The grin is cocky and dangerous, an exaggerated cartoon stunt.
1.2–3.2s: camera pulls far back along the axe's flight. He launches it toward a gigantic suspended iron bell twenty feet away. The chain unreels as ONE visible connected line from his hand to the axe. The axe hooks over the bell's top handle rather than chopping anything. He plants both boots in his airborne graphic pose and yanks, swinging the enormous bell across frame like a pendulum. Pure cyan surrounds every object, no support structure, floor or scenery.
3.2–4.8s: the first bell slams broadside into a second smaller iron bell, physically ringing both. An orange fire pulse races visibly down the chain, engulfs only the first bell in a tight ink-edged flame wreath, then jumps across their contact into the second bell a fraction of a second later. Two distinct escalating booms make the CHAIN REACTION readable; the second bell launches backward with a giant bounded orange/ivory impact star and long disconnected tapered trails. No people hit, no body damage, no full-screen fire or smoke.
4.8–6s: snap back as he recalls the chained axe in a clean corkscrew and catches the handle. Exact title CHAIN REACTION drops heavily beside his upper body and settles without obscuring his face. The chain is metal, never a fist-shaped effect.
6–8s: clear whole-character ending with axe resting over his shoulder, one small finite flame licking its head. He pinches that last flame out between two gloved fingertips, then flicks one harmless ember away. His grim grin stays fixed. SFX: heavy chain rattle, building metal whistle, two enormous staggered bell impacts, fast traveling fire rush, chain recall, title slam and tiny flame snuff. No speech, music or narration.

name: Regular guy named LeBron James
qaNote: Reference inspected. This is the game's fictional regular guy, preserve his reference face instead of substituting the athlete. Preserve dark tank top and existing shirt wording, black jeans and boots. Review refrigerator/bag hand continuity, dramatic distance, exact title, intact groceries and navy fabric chroma key.
choreography:
IDENTITY: the FICTIONAL regular guy in the reference: young adult dark-skinned muscular man, short tight black curls, clean-shaven angular face, dark navy tank top with its existing white shirt slogan, black jeans, black belt and black lace-up work boots. Use this exact illustrated face, not a different celebrity likeness. Preserve the source shirt lettering as a fixed costume detail; the only NEW on-screen wording is the move title. No sports uniform, crown or basketball court.
0–1.2s: establish complete character casually carrying one brown grocery bag in his left arm. A single egg pops upward from the bag. He looks annoyed and reaches for it with his right hand. Camera whips upward to reveal an enormous tumbling ivory refrigerator descending toward the egg and groceries. Treat this as a completely absurd graphic prop stunt on empty cyan.
1.2–3.2s: camera pulls WAY back to show the refrigerator is three times taller than him. In one explosive leap he intercepts it with his right palm while keeping the grocery bag upright in his left arm. The refrigerator compresses slightly with cartoon squash at the hand contact, one huge ivory/orange bounded pressure burst behind it. Hold the impossible one-handed catch for a tiny emphatic beat, then drive into the reversal. Face strained with annoyance, not triumph.
3.2–4.8s: he rotates his whole body into a colossal one-arm throw, sending the refrigerator thirty feet away into an enormous open cardboard shipping carton. Track its accelerating flight in depth, then the clean direct impact. The carton folds its flaps around the refrigerator in four thunderous CLACKS and shoots off into distant cyan, intact. This is the huge finisher payoff, not a gentle set-down. Grocery bag remains in his left arm without changing hands; no people endangered.
4.8–6s: camera snap-zooms back to his irritated face as he comes into a complete upright hero composition. His now-free right hand catches the SAME egg just before it falls back into the grocery bag. Exact title DEFINITELY NOT HIM slams below his shoulders with heavy comic impact.
6–8s: pull back enough to show his entire character, grocery bag secure, egg perfectly intact. He raises one eyebrow toward the camera, slowly points to the existing message on his own tank top, then gives a dry exhausted head shake. Crisp character comedy after the absurd feat. SFX: little egg pop, plunging refrigerator rush, gigantic palm-stop impact, explosive launch whoosh, distant carton thunder and four flap clacks, title slam, tiny soft egg catch and bag rustle. No dialogue, music, crowd or scenery.
